concepts.name: Continuous versus discrete-time signals
concepts.summary: Distinguish signals defined for all real time x(t) from sequences x[n] defined only at integer indices, and give examples of each.

concepts.name: Basic signal operations
concepts.summary: Explain how shifting, reversing and scaling the time axis and scaling amplitude change the graph of a signal.

concepts.name: Standard test signals
concepts.summary: Recognise and sketch the unit step, ramp, rectangular pulse, real and complex exponentials and sinusoids.

concepts.name: Unit impulse function
concepts.summary: Explain the continuous delta and discrete unit sample and the sifting property that lets a signal be built from shifted impulses.

concepts.name: Even, odd and periodic signals
concepts.summary: Classify a signal as even, odd or periodic and identify its period or fundamental frequency.

concepts.name: System as input-output mapping
concepts.summary: Describe a system as a rule that maps an input signal to an output signal, with examples such as an RC circuit or a moving average.

concepts.name: Energy and power of signals
concepts.summary: Explain energy and average power of a signal and distinguish energy signals from power signals.

misconceptions.text: A discrete-time signal is just a continuous signal with small steps, so it is defined between the integer sample points.
The unit impulse is a very tall pulse whose value at zero is simply infinity, so it has no defined meaning.
The sum of any two periodic signals is always periodic.

concepts.name: Linearity and time invariance
concepts.summary: Test a given system for linearity and time invariance by applying superposition and input shifts.

concepts.name: Impulse response
concepts.summary: Explain that the response of an LTI system to a unit impulse fully characterises the system.

concepts.name: Causality and stability of systems
concepts.summary: Determine whether a system is causal, memoryless or BIBO stable from its equation or response.

concepts.name: Convolution integral and sum
concepts.summary: Compute the output of an LTI system by flipping, shifting, multiplying and integrating or summing for simple signals.

concepts.name: Convolution properties
concepts.summary: Apply commutativity, associativity and distributivity of convolution to combine cascaded and parallel systems.

concepts.name: Step response
concepts.summary: Obtain the step response as the running integral or sum of the impulse response and read off settling behaviour.

concepts.name: Difference and differential equations
concepts.summary: Describe simple LTI systems with linear constant-coefficient equations and find homogeneous and particular solutions.

concepts.name: Complex exponentials as eigenfunctions
concepts.summary: Explain that an LTI system maps e^{st} or z^n to a scaled copy of itself, motivating frequency-domain analysis.

misconceptions.text: A system whose output is a straight line in the input, such as y = 2x + 3, is linear.
Convolution is just pointwise multiplication of the input and the impulse response.
A bounded impulse response is enough for BIBO stability.

concepts.name: Fourier series representation
concepts.summary: Compute Fourier series coefficients of periodic signals and reconstruct them from harmonics.

concepts.name: Continuous-time Fourier transform
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret the Fourier transform of common aperiodic signals using the definition and tables.

concepts.name: Fourier transform properties
concepts.summary: Use linearity, time shift, modulation, scaling, differentiation and the convolution theorem to find transforms and outputs.

concepts.name: Frequency response of LTI systems
concepts.summary: Relate the frequency response to the impulse response and predict the output of a system for sinusoidal inputs.

concepts.name: Laplace transform and ROC
concepts.summary: Compute Laplace transforms and inverse transforms, tracking the region of convergence for causal and anticausal signals.

concepts.name: Transfer function poles and zeros
concepts.summary: Derive a transfer function from a differential equation and infer stability and causality from pole locations and ROC.

concepts.name: Discrete-time Fourier transform
concepts.summary: Compute the DTFT of sequences and explain why it is periodic in frequency with period 2π.

concepts.name: z-transform and ROC
concepts.summary: Compute z-transforms and inverses, link pole positions relative to the unit circle to stability, and solve difference equations.

misconceptions.text: The Fourier transform of a signal exists for every signal, including growing exponentials.
The Laplace transform expression alone identifies the signal, without specifying the region of convergence.
A system with a pole in the right half-plane is always unstable, regardless of the ROC.

concepts.name: Sampling theorem and aliasing
concepts.summary: Analyse the spectrum of an impulse-sampled signal to show when reconstruction is possible and how aliasing arises.

concepts.name: Ideal and practical reconstruction
concepts.summary: Compare sinc interpolation with zero-order hold and quantify the distortion each introduces.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform and FFT
concepts.summary: Relate the DFT to samples of the DTFT and analyse leakage, resolution and zero padding in spectral estimates.

concepts.name: Circular versus linear convolution
concepts.summary: Analyse when DFT multiplication yields linear convolution and choose transform lengths to avoid wraparound.

concepts.name: Filter specification and design
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs among passband ripple, transition width and stopband attenuation when choosing a filter.

concepts.name: FIR and IIR filter structures
concepts.summary: Compare FIR and IIR filters in terms of stability, phase linearity, order and computational cost.

concepts.name: Group delay and phase distortion
concepts.summary: Analyse how nonlinear phase response distorts waveforms through group delay variation.

concepts.name: Bode plots and system response
concepts.summary: Sketch and interpret Bode plots for first- and second-order systems and relate them to time-domain response.

misconceptions.text: Sampling at exactly twice the highest frequency always guarantees perfect reconstruction.
Aliasing can be removed digitally after sampling.
Zero padding before a DFT increases the true frequency resolution.

concepts.name: Time-frequency uncertainty trade-off
concepts.summary: Evaluate how limits on joint time and frequency localisation constrain analysis, windowing and filter design.

concepts.name: Optimal filter design methods
concepts.summary: Design FIR and IIR filters to meet specifications using equiripple, window and bilinear methods and justify the choice.

concepts.name: Multirate signal processing
concepts.summary: Evaluate and design sample-rate conversion systems, including anti-aliasing and anti-imaging filters.

concepts.name: State-space representation
concepts.summary: Model LTI systems in state-space form and relate eigenvalues of the state matrix to transfer function poles and stability.

concepts.name: Stochastic signals and spectra
concepts.summary: Evaluate how random signals and noise are shaped by LTI systems using autocorrelation and power spectral density.

concepts.name: Matched and Wiener filtering
concepts.summary: Design filters that maximise signal-to-noise ratio or minimise mean-square error for a stated signal and noise model.

concepts.name: Time-frequency and wavelet analysis
concepts.summary: Judge when short-time Fourier or wavelet methods are more appropriate than global Fourier analysis for nonstationary signals.

concepts.name: Finite word-length effects
concepts.summary: Assess how quantisation of coefficients and arithmetic affects filter performance and choose structures to mitigate it.

misconceptions.text: A transform that is sharper in both time and frequency can always be obtained with a better window.
Decimating a signal by M is just discarding samples, with no need for prior filtering.
A filter designed with infinite-precision coefficients will behave identically when implemented in fixed-point arithmetic.
